b: Ahead of the release of his latest album for Warp Records, All Ages, the Italian artist discusses the skateboarding and hardcore music culture that inspired him as a teenager, and the act of rebellion he took against himself in making the new LP

With a population of around 1,000 people, Lorenzo Senni’s childhood village of Ronta wasn’t especially a thriving hub for cultural activity when he was growing up. While it wasn’t far from the more active nearby cities of Cesena and Rimini, where he occasionally visited as an impressionable teen, its leisurely way of living made for a generation of young people desperate to find new hobbies and something out of the ordinary.
